summary: ASTRAHEALTH is a space-focused crew health monitoring prototype designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. It brings together physical health monitoring, mental wellness assessment, radiation monitoring, and AI-assisted health analysis in a single dashboard. The system presents health information through visual indicators, alerts, and reports to help identify potential health concerns. ASTRAHEALTH aims to demonstrate how an integrated digital health monitoring platform could support crew safety and informed decision-making during space exploration.
details:
ASTRAHEALTH – Astronaut Health Monitoring and Assessment System

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

ASTRAHEALTH is a Streamlit-based astronaut health monitoring and assessment prototype designed to support crew well-being during space missions. It brings different aspects of astronaut health into a single, organized dashboard.

The system consists of six modules:

  • Dashboard: Provides an overview of crew health information and alerts.
  • Physical Health: Presents physical health information for monitoring.
  • Mental Health: Provides a self-report check-in covering mood, perceived stress and sleep quality.
  • Radiation Monitoring: Presents radiation exposure information to increase awareness of this spaceflight hazard.
  • AI Health Analysis: Uses rule-based logic to identify potential health concerns based on available information.
  • Health Reports: Organizes health information for review.

The overall approach is to present health information in an understandable format, highlight potential concerns and support further assessment when necessary.

2. What are its benefits and intended impact?

Spaceflight can expose astronauts to several challenges, including physical changes, radiation exposure, psychological stress and sleep disturbances. ASTRAHEALTH aims to make different aspects of crew health easier to monitor and understand through one interface.

Its intended benefits include:

  • Bringing multiple health-related indicators together in one dashboard.
  • Encouraging awareness of physical and mental well-being.
  • Helping users recognize potential health concerns.
  • Organizing health information for easier review.
  • Providing a foundation for future astronaut health monitoring solutions.

The long-term goal is to support astronaut health awareness and contribute to safer, more informed decision-making during long-duration space missions.

3. What technologies and tools were used?

The project was developed using:

  • Python: Main programming language.
  • Streamlit: Development of the interactive web application.
  • Pandas: Handling and organizing health-related data.
  • Plotly: Visual presentation of information and charts.
  • Arduino IDE: Used in our separate hardware experimentation for the fire and hazardous gas detection project, not as an ASTRAHEALTH component.

ASTRAHEALTH is accessible through a web browser and does not currently require specialized hardware.

4. What makes the project creative?

ASTRAHEALTH combines physical health, mental wellness, radiation awareness and rule-based health analysis in a single astronaut-focused interface.

Instead of presenting health information as disconnected measurements, the project organizes it into dedicated modules within a mission-control-inspired dashboard. Its design focuses on making information accessible and understandable.

The combination of different health monitoring areas provides a foundation that can be expanded with interactive features, historical trends and real-time measurements in future versions.

5. What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered the importance of astronaut health during long-duration space missions, the effects of spaceflight hazards, ease of understanding health indicators and the need to organize different types of health information in one place.

We also considered the importance of identifying potential concerns early and making information accessible to both crew members and medical professionals.

6. Future improvements

Future development could include real-time wearable and medical sensor integration, historical health trend analysis, scheduled health check-ins, improved risk assessment and secure communication between astronauts and flight surgeons.

Current implementation note: ASTRAHEALTH is a demonstration prototype using sample or manually entered information. It does not connect to live NASA systems, spacecraft sensors or medical devices. Its AI Health Analysis module uses rule-based logic rather than a trained machine-learning model. It is not a clinically validated diagnostic system.
